app.tagline: A lean NAS operating system that boots from a USB stick and runs entirely in RAM.
lang.label: Language
auth.name: Name
auth.setupIntro: Create the first account. It is the owner of this NAS and has full rights.
auth.nameHint: You sign in with this name. Lowercase letters, digits, - and _, starting with a letter.
auth.passwordMismatch: The two passwords do not match.
auth.rateLimited: Too many failed attempts. Try again in {seconds} seconds.
error.invalid_name: The name must start with a lowercase letter and may only contain a–z, 0–9, - and _ (at most 32 characters).
error.reserved_name: This name is reserved for the system. Choose another one.
error.setup_done: The owner account already exists. Sign in instead.
error.config_unavailable: The stick with the configuration is not reachable.
error.config_write_failed: That could not be saved to the stick.
error.unreachable: The NAS is not reachable right now.
error.unauthorized: You are no longer signed in.
error.forbidden: This account does not have the rights for that.
error.unsupported_type: This file format is not supported.
error.internal: That did not work. The log on the NAS has the details.
config.missingText: TitanOS cannot read its configuration. Is the USB stick named TITANOS plugged in? Without it nobody can sign in and nothing is saved.
unreachable.title: NAS not reachable
unreachable.text: The web UI gets no answer from the NAS. Is it running and on the network?
nav.label: Main navigation
power.servicesNote: All running services are stopped cleanly.
power.restartNote: Takes about 1–2 minutes. The web UI reconnects by itself afterwards.
power.shutdownNote: To turn it on again, press the button on the device.
power.restartingText: This page reloads as soon as the NAS is reachable again.
dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.editHint: Move tiles by their handle, resize them at the corner. Everything snaps to a grid of 12 columns.
dashboard.hiddenHint: The layout is saved for your account. On narrow screens the tiles are stacked automatically.
dashboard.unsaved: Edit mode · changes not saved yet
placeholder.title: Not available yet
placeholder.text: This area follows in a later version of TitanOS.
settings.title: Settings
settings.appearanceDesc: Themes, colors, glass effect, corners, font size and background.
appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.intro: Saved for your account. You see every change in the preview right away.
appearance.importFailed: This file is not a TitanOS theme.
appearance.contrastWarning: Text on surfaces only has a contrast of {ratio} – at least 4.5:1 reads well.
appearance.accentHint: Also used for the frame of the logo and the “OS” in the wordmark.
appearance.glassHint: Glass only shows with a background behind it. Text always stays on a surface that is opaque enough – too much transparency is limited automatically.
appearance.radiusCtl: Corners of buttons, fields and menus
appearance.imageHint: Upload your own image (JPG, PNG, WebP, up to 10 MB). It is stored in /config.
appearance.previewAutoDark: System is dark right now → Graphite
appearance.previewAutoLight: System is light right now → Light
appearance.previewDefault: This is how TitanOS looks for you
error.invalid_volume_name: The name must start with a lowercase letter and may only contain a–z, 0–9 and - (at most 12 characters).
error.volume_exists: A volume with this name already exists.
error.volume_not_found: This volume does not exist (any more).
error.invalid_level: This RAID level is not supported.
error.too_few_disks: Too few disks are selected for this RAID level.
error.disk_unavailable: One of the disks is not available (any more). Rescan the disks.
error.not_confirmed: Erasing the data was not confirmed.
error.volume_busy: The volume is in use and cannot be unmounted.
error.not_possible: That is not possible in the volume's current state.
error.storage_failed: A system command failed. The state of the disks is shown below; details:
storage.title: Storage
storage.noVolumesHint: A volume combines several disks into one storage, protected against the failure of one or two disks depending on the RAID level.
storage.removeDiskConfirm: Remove {disk} from the volume {volume}? The disk is wiped and free afterwards.
sync.rebuilding: {disks} is being added to the volume
sync.rebuildingNote: Until this is finished redundancy is reduced: another failure can now cost data.
sync.syncing: The disks are being synchronized for the first time
sync.syncingNote: The volume can already be used.
sync.checking: All copies and parity are read and compared
storage.degradedNote: At least one disk is missing. The data is still there, but redundancy is reduced. Add a replacement disk.
storage.failedNote: Too many disks are missing, the volume is not running. Do not change anything on the disks before it is clear what happened.
storage.missingNote: None of this volume's disks were found. Are they connected?
storage.freeHint: Free disks contain no partitions. You can create a new volume from them or add them to a volume as a spare that steps in automatically when a disk fails.
create.title: New volume
create.name: Name
create.nameHint: Lowercase letters, digits and -, at most 12 characters. The volume is mounted at /mnt/<name>.
create.disksNone: There is no disk that can be used.
create.capacityEven: select an even number of disks
create.raid0Warning: RAID 0 has no redundancy. If a single disk fails, all data of the volume is lost.
create.eraseConfirm: All data on {disks} will be erased for good.
level.raid0Desc: Fast, full size, no protection. 2 disks or more.
level.raid1Desc: Mirror: every disk holds everything. 2 disks or more.
level.raid5Desc: One disk may fail. 3 disks or more.
level.raid6Desc: Two disks may fail. 4 disks or more.
level.raid10Desc: Mirrored pairs, fast. 4 disks or more, even number.
fs.xfsDesc: Good for large files and large volumes.
addDisk.title: Add a disk to {volume}
addDisk.rebuild: The volume is missing a disk. The new disk takes its place and is rebuilt right away.
addDisk.spare: The volume is complete. The disk becomes a spare and steps in automatically when another one fails.
addDisk.eraseConfirm: All data on {disk} will be erased for good.
delete.title: Delete the volume {volume}?
delete.warning: All data on the volume will be erased for good. The disks are empty and free afterwards.
delete.typeName: Type the name of the volume to confirm:
error.read_only: Disks are not changed in development mode.
error.user_not_found: This account does not exist (any more).
error.user_exists: An account with this name already exists.
error.last_owner: There always has to be at least one owner.
error.cannot_delete_self: You cannot delete the account you are signed in with.
error.rate_limited: Too many failed attempts. Wait a moment.
error.invalid_share_name: The name may only contain a–z, 0–9, - and _ and be at most 32 characters long.
error.share_exists: A share with this name already exists.
error.share_not_found: This share does not exist (any more).
error.unknown_user: One of the accounts does not exist (any more).
error.invalid_nfs_client: NFS needs at least one host or network, e.g. 192.168.1.0/24. Names, addresses and networks are allowed.
error.invalid_option: A value is out of range.
error.volume_change: A share cannot move to another volume.
error.volume_has_shares: The volume still holds shares. Delete them first.
users.title: Users
users.name: Name
users.smbPending: SMB only after the next sign-in to the web UI
users.passwordNote: The password is used for the web UI and for SMB shares. Other devices signed in with the old password are signed out.
users.deleteText: The account, its settings and its access to all shares are removed. Files in the shares are kept.
shares.title: Shares
shares.emptyHint: A share is a folder on a volume that computers on the network can open over SMB or NFS.
shares.needVolume: A share needs a volume first.
share.name: Name
share.nameHint: The name of the share on the network. Lowercase letters, digits, - and _.
share.smb: SMB – for Windows, macOS and Linux, with sign-in
share.nfs: NFS – for Linux and devices without sign-in
share.nfsClients: Allowed hosts or networks, one per line
share.nfsWarning: NFS knows no accounts: whoever sits at one of these hosts can read and write in the share.
share.guest: Guest access: anyone on the network may read without a password
share.guestWarning: With guest access every device on your network can read all files of this share.
share.recycle: Recycle bin: keep files deleted over SMB
share.timeMachine: Offer as a Time Machine target
share.timeMachineSize: Size limit in GB (0 = no limit)
share.deleteText: The share is removed. The files stay in {path} and are not deleted.
